A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ROGR research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original ROGR evaluations on TensoIR and Stanford-ORB, component and sensitivity ablations, and qualitative real-object and normal-map renderings.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results in Tables 1–2, ablations in Tables 3–4, and qualitative rendering results.

M1.justification: The multi-view relighting diffusion model and NeRF with general and specular conditioning remain unchanged. Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same architecture, objectives and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Training sources, TensoIR and Stanford-ORB evaluations, and real-object captures are unchanged. Removing selected normal-map illustrations does not remove those objects from the retained benchmark evaluation.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same comparator sets, including IllumiNeRF, Neural Gaffer, R3DG and the inverse-rendering baselines. Partially obscured labels in v2 Figure 5 are a layout issue, not comparator removal.

E3.justification: Splits, evaluation views and illuminations, metrics, normalization procedures and training settings are unchanged. Benchmark protocol details move from Appendix C.2 into Section 4.1; the new metrics subsection repeats existing information.

E4.justification: The normal-map geometry inspection is reduced from four objects in v1 Figure 8 to hotdog and Lego in v2 Figure 7, omitting ficus and armadillo. Component, resolution, view-count and illumination-count ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: The ficus and armadillo normal-map renderings are removed. Numerical benchmark and ablation results are unchanged, including TensoIR PSNR 30.74 and the default hotdog ablation PSNR 31.88; splitting the ablation table adds no new measurements.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4) and Appendix B.2's rendering formulation retain the same mathematical content. No assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: generative multi-view relighting distilled into a lighting-conditioned NeRF, arbitrary-illumination inference without additional optimization, and strong benchmark performance.

C2.justification: Ablation interpretations and limitations concerning complex materials, distant illumination and object-centric scenes are unchanged. The normal-map quality interpretation moves from Appendix D.1 into Section 5.4 without substantive revision.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendices B–C retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing, capture procedures and data-release statement. Relocated benchmark details are not new disclosures.

R1.justification: The same 64 references remain. Section 2 qualifies its characterization of RelitLRM: v1 says it fails to maintain consistent geometry, whereas v2 says it does not guarantee consistency across environment maps.

P1.justification: Existing benchmark details and normal-map discussion move into the main text, metrics receive a separate subsection, and an appendix heading is added. Related-work wording and a typo are edited, while most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v1 Table 3 becomes v2 Tables 3–4, separating component ablations from view and illumination counts. Figures are resized or relocated, and the normal-map figure loses two rows. Figure 5's caption overlap is fixed, but the Neural Gaffer and Neural-PBIR labels become partially obscured.

improvement.justification: v2 improves navigation through existing evaluation details, separates ablation groups and makes Figure 5's full caption visible. However, it removes normal-map evidence for two objects and partially obscures baseline labels. With the method and quantitative evidence unchanged, these competing changes in readability and qualitative support do not establish a clear net quality improvement or deterioration.
